text:
maria: @sre-oncall FYI customer BrightDocs reporting widespread 5xx/timeouts on hosted inference since 12:03 UTC. saw p95 jump to ~2.8s and p99 tail >20s. sample req id req_bd_9f3, tenant=brightdocs-prod. logs point to request queue depth hitting 2048 and continuous-batcher backlog climbing rapidly. :rotating_light:

maria: repro steps they ran (from customer) — small loop hitting our text-gen endpoint with concurrency 20:```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-l32k","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}' \
  -w '\nHTTP %{http_code} in %{time_total}s\n' -s -o /dev/null
```

sre-oncall: thanks — can you paste the exact timestamps and any request ids? also: did they mention any recent model pins or quantization changes? :thinking_face:

maria: timeframe 12:03:12 -> 12:12:45 UTC, attached two sample request ids: req_bd_9f3 and req_bd_9f8. customer said they didn't change anything. they did notice spikes correlate with a scheduled job that kicks off hourly (bulk indexer).

kevin: quick check: deploy-bot shows a config push at 11:58 UTC to hosted routing (tiny traffic shuffles). not sure if related. deploy-bot: "config-rollout/hosted-routing v12 -> v13 by ops-team at 2023-11-08T11:58:09Z"

sre-oncall: looking at infra metrics — continuous-batcher queue length graph for cluster hosted-eu-west shows sustained climb starting 12:00, queue_depth = 2048 (our soft limit), dequeue rate throttled. KV cache misses spiked at same time. p95/kernel timeouts present.

support: customer notes their retries increased after initial 502s which amplified load. they say client had backoff of 100ms fixed which made it worse. attaching their request trace: trace_brightdocs_0001.

maria: logs snippet from gateway at 12:05:```
[2023-11-08T12:05:02Z] tenant=brightdocs-prod req=req_bd_9f3  upstream=hosted-batcher-9 err=queue_depth_limit msg="enqueue rejected" status=503
[2023-11-08T12:05:03Z] tenant=brightdocs-prod req=req_bd_9f4  upstream=hosted-batcher-11 err=dequeue-delay msg="dequeue wait 9.8s" status=504
[2023-11-08T12:05:04Z] tenant=brightdocs-prod kv_miss=1 queue_len=1987 backlog=1200 p95=2.74s
```

sre-oncall: immediate mitigation options:
- throttle tenant to 10 rps (rate-limit)
- temporarily increase queue soft limit to 4096 for hosted-eu-west (risk: memory spike)
- enable fallback routing to smaller model (open-l7b) to reduce batch size
- ask customer to increase client backoff to exponential (250ms base)

kevin: let's do tenant throttle + fallback routing. i'll open a quick rollback of recent routing config if we still see pressure after throttle.

maria: executing tenant throttle now (support portal change): set brightdocs-prod rate limit 10rps.

sre-oncall: confirmed throttle applied at 12:07:10 UTC. queue depth started to drop but backlog still >600. initiating fallback routing to open-l7b for that tenant.

maria: applied routing override to pin tenant->open-l7b with autoscale pool at 2x to handle throughput at 12:08:05 UTC.

deploy-bot: "routing-override brightdocs-prod -> open-l7b by maria at 2023-11-08T12:08:05Z"

support: customer reports errors decreased after 12:10 but still seeing p95 ~1.2s. they're asking for postmortem and why our queue hit soft limit. :wave:

sre-oncall: notes for triage: need to investigate causes of sudden KV cache miss storm and why dequeue rate couldn't keep up. suspects: batcher slow-path due to model memory thrash after routing change (v12->v13) or the hourly bulk job created synchronized bursts.

kevin: followups:
- collect block traces for batcher containers (12:00-12:12) -> /var/logs/hosted-eu-west/batcher-traces.tar.gz
- capture kernel scheduling/alloc logs for those times -> perf dump
- check model variant selector logs for fallback decisions
- ask product to review routing v12->v13 diff (small change to shard preferencer)

maria: support thread to customer: "we applied a temporary rate-limit and routed you to a smaller model; errors should be reduced while we investigate root cause. we'll follow up with timeline + action items." :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: post-incident actions proposed:
1) add per-tenant early-slowdown policy when queue_len > 1500 (graceful shed)
2) increase alarm sensitivity for KV-miss rate + consumer dequeue rate mismatch
3) rehearse runbook for continuous-batcher backlog (fast mitigation steps)
4) revisit default client retry/backoff docs in DevEx

kevin: i'll start the runbook write-up and include command snippets for quick throttle, routing override, and queue soft-limit bump.

maria: thanks all — will update incident ticket INC-8421 with logs and mitigation notes.
